title: Growing Experiments
strapline: Does a seed need light? Does it need water? Set up the test, wait, and let the plants answer.
intent: Setting up growing experiments — a seed with water and one without, one in light and one in the dark — turns planting into real, testable science.
Predicting what a plant needs, then watching over days and weeks to see who was right, teaches children about living things and about patient, longitudinal observation.
Planting, watering and tending build fine-motor care and a sense of responsibility for something living.
Comparing the results — this one grew tall, this one stayed small, this one died — invites reasoning about cause and about what plants need to thrive.
The slow, unfolding change over time helps children grasp growth, sequence and the passing of days and weeks.
Growing food or flowers children then use or enjoy closes a satisfying loop from seed to harvest.
implementation: Set up fair tests together — identical beans in identical pots, changing just one thing: water, light or warmth.
Ask for predictions and record them: 'which one do you think will grow? why?' — then watch and check over the days.
Use fast, reliable growers — cress, beans, sunflowers — so children see change without losing interest.
Photograph or measure the plants regularly and line the records up so children can see and discuss the change.
Talk about what living things need, drawing out children's reasoning from what the plants actually did.
Grow something children can use — cress for sandwiches, flowers for the table — to reward the waiting.
key_questions: Which one do you think will grow — and why?
What do you think this plant needs to stay alive?
How has it changed since we last measured it?
Why did this one grow tall and this one stay small?
What would happen if we didn't water it at all?

impact.text: Children set up fair tests and watch over days and weeks — real, testable science and patient observation.

Children compare the results and reason about what plants need to thrive.
Children measure and record the plants over time, grasping growth, sequence and the passing of days.
Children grow food or flowers they then use, closing a loop from seed to harvest.

playing_exploring: Children plant, water and tend, exploring soil, seeds and the tools of growing at first hand.

active_learning: Tending plants over days and weeks builds real responsibility and the patience to wait for a slow result.
creating_thinking: Children predict what a plant needs, test it fairly, and reason from the results about what made the difference.
